Shasta County Superior Court: A Comprehensive Guide

Quick Reference Information

Main Address:
1500 Court St
Redding, CA 96001
United States

Phone: (530) 245-6789
Website: www.shasta.courts.ca.gov

Hours of Operation:
Monday – Friday: 8:30 AM – 4:00 PM
Saturday & Sunday: Closed

Overview

The Shasta County Superior Court, established in 1850, serves as the primary judicial institution in Shasta County, California. With three main facilities and 14 modern courtrooms built in 2010, the court upholds its mission to provide fair, equal, and just justice to all residents.

Court Locations

1. Main Courthouse

Address: 1500 Court St, Redding, CA 96001 Phone: (530) 245-6789

Handles:

  • Civil cases
  • Family law
  • Probate matters
  • Small claims
  • Criminal cases
  • Traffic violations
  • Some juvenile dependency cases

2. Justice Center

Address: 1655 West Street, Redding, CA 96001 Phone: (530) 245-6789

Specializes in:

  • Criminal cases
  • Traffic violations
  • Appeals

3. Juvenile Justice Center

Address: 2680 Radio Lane, Redding, CA 96001 Phone: (530) 245-6481

Focuses on:

  • Juvenile dependency cases
  • Juvenile delinquency matters
  • Adoptions

Services and Features

Online Services

  • Case information search
  • Document access
  • Fine payments
  • Forms download
  • Traffic school registration
  • Jury summons information

Case Search Options

  1. Search by:
    • Record/case number
    • Ticket/citation number
    • First and last name
    • Business name
    • Attorney information
    • Judicial officer
    • Courtroom

Payment Methods

  1. In-Person
    • Cash
    • Checks
    • Credit/debit cards (2.5% surcharge applies)
  2. Online
    • Through court portal
    • Credit/debit cards
  3. By Mail
    • Certified checks
    • Money orders
    • Send to: 1500 Court St, Redding, CA 96001
  4. By Phone
    • Call (530) 245-6789
    • Have citation number ready

Remote Hearings

  • Conducted via Zoom
  • Advance registration required
  • Join 10 minutes before scheduled time
  • Audio and video testing recommended
  • Microphone muting required until called

Court Departments and Services

Small Claims Division

  • Maximum claim amount: $10,000
  • Quick resolution process
  • Cases must involve county residents

Family Law Services

  • Divorce proceedings
  • Child custody and support
  • Domestic violence cases
  • Elder abuse cases
  • Spousal support
  • Workplace harassment

Criminal Division

  • Misdemeanors
  • Felonies
  • Warrants
  • Traffic violations

Important Policies

Court Attendance

  • Proper dress required
  • Mask wearing mandatory
  • Follow local court rules
  • Arrive on time

Record Requests

  • Public records available
  • Some records restricted
  • Fees apply per page
  • In-person requests may be required

FAQs

Q: How do I file a case?
A: Visit the courthouse or use the online filing system.

Q: How can I access court records?
A: Use the online portal or visit in person.

Q: How do I request an interpreter?
A: Contact Interpreter Services department directly.

Q: Is legal assistance available?
A: Yes, through self-help centers and legal assistance programs.

Q: What if I need to make payments in installments?
A: Contact the Court Collection Division. Minimum monthly payment is $50.
